reuse.why: Adds a shared skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate and reuses getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend, but no single shared function applies the full skip-or-move rule, so each site wires it up itself.

duplication.why: The 'filter weekend days if daily, else move with getDateWithSkippedWeekend' logic is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the schedule-template loop, along with the WEEKDAY_LOOKAHEAD over-fetch.

placement.why: The predicate and lookahead constant live in shared/schedules where the weekend rules live, though the application of the rule is spread into server/schedules/app.ts and budget/schedule-template.ts.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the weekend rule's call sites, the frequency passthrough, tests, docs and a release note.

maintainability.why: A future change to weekend handling must be mirrored across three hand-rolled skip/move implementations with subtly different shapes (one site relies on getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag being inverted).

disguised_duplication.where: Skip-or-move logic reshaped three ways: .find(!isWeekend) + ternary in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, .filter(!isWeekend).slice + ternary in server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates, getEffectiveDate closure in budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList.

one_place.where: Only the 'is daily with skipWeekend' predicate is shared (skipsWeekendOccurrences); the skip-vs-move application is reimplemented in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.ts.
